children: Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has announced its unaudited results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026, reporting its highest-ever Q2 room rates, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit. Growth was driven by its owned hotels and managed and franchised portfolio.

For Q2 FY27, total revenue grew 18 per cent to Rs 363.8 crore, and net EBITDA increased 22 per cent to Rs 162.2 crore, with net EBITDA margin rising 157 bps to 44.6 per cent. Before the impact of GST changes and the provision for stock appreciation rights, which together came to 3.2 per cent of revenue, net EBITDA grew 31 per cent to Rs 173.7 crore, with a margin of 47.7 per cent.

PBT before exceptional items grew 59 per cent to Rs 88.8 crore, PAT increased 90 per cent to Rs 79.8 crore, and cash profit rose 28 per cent to Rs 97.2 crore. RevPAR grew 18 per cent to Rs 5,137, supported by an 8 per cent increase in average room rate to Rs 6,751 and a 633-bps gain in occupancy to 76.1 per cent. Owned hotels recorded 15 per cent revenue growth to Rs 337 crore, while hotel EBITDAR margin increased 112 bps to 53 per cent.

Commenting on the results, Neelendra Singh, Managing Director, Lemon Tree Hotels, said, “Q2 has been a strong quarter for Lemon Tree Hotels, with our highest-ever Q2 revenue, EBITDA and profitability. Revenue grew by 18 per cent and Net EBITDA grew 22 per cent, with margins expanding by 157 basis points while absorbing the impact of GST changes and stock appreciation rights. Room rates grew by 8 per cent and occupancy climbed by more than six percentage points to 76.1 per cent.

The simultaneous growth in room rates and occupancy reflects the strength of our brands and the effectiveness of our distribution network and loyalty programme in bringing guests back. Together, these are the engines driving performance across our portfolio and also creating value for our owner partners. We signed 825 rooms and opened 523 rooms in Q2; while fees from third-party hotels grew 30 per cent. As the New India Traveller seeks increasingly differentiated hospitality experiences, our pipeline is expanding in step with this demand, such as Aurika in Shimla, Shillong and Varanasi to Lemon Tree Premier in Bandra, Mumbai.”

For H1 FY27, total revenue grew 14 per cent to Rs 710.6 crore, net EBITDA increased 14 per cent to Rs 314.0 crore, PAT rose 52 per cent to Rs 137.1 crore, and cash profit grew 22 per cent to Rs 193.2 crore. Management fees increased 20 per cent to Rs 86.1 crore, comprising Rs 41.5 crore from third-party-owned hotels, up 36 per cent, and Rs 44.7 crore from Fleur Hotels, up 8 per cent.

RevPAR grew across every brand in the owned portfolio: Aurika recorded 17 per cent growth, Lemon Tree Premier 18 per cent, Lemon Tree Hotels 15 per cent, Red Fox 21 per cent and Keys 29 per cent. Aurika and Lemon Tree Premier together contributed 63 per cent of owned-hotel EBITDAR on 58 per cent of revenue, with Aurika recording a hotel EBITDAR margin of 59 per cent. The Keys portfolio delivered a hotel EBITDAR margin of 50 per cent. Fees from third-party-owned hotels grew 30 per cent to Rs 18.7 crore, while total network revenue across owned, managed and franchised hotels increased 23 per cent to Rs 573 crore.

During Q2, the company opened eight managed and franchised hotels with 523 rooms and signed 11 hotels with 825 rooms, about 1.6 times the inventory opened during the quarter. As of September 30, 2026, its combined operational and pipeline portfolio stood at 285 hotels and 24,061 rooms across 170+ cities. Of these, 138 hotels with 12,131 rooms across 80+ cities were operational.

The company acquired land in Bandra (East), Mumbai, next to BKC, for about Rs 120 crore to develop Lemon Tree Premier, Bandra, an owned 172-room upscale hotel. It will be the group’s seventh hotel in Mumbai and its first in Bandra, with opening expected in FY30. Aurika, Shimla, an owned 90-room hotel, is expected to open in FY27, followed by Aurika, Shillong (165 rooms) in FY28 and Aurika, Varanasi (47 rooms, heritage) in FY29.

Gross debt as of September 30, 2026, stood at Rs 1,429.2 crore, down 11 per cent from Rs 1,610.2 crore a year earlier. Cost of debt fell 28 bps to 7.44 per cent, while debt to equity improved to 0.64x from 0.86x.

On the ESG front, 100 per cent of the company’s 41 owned and leased hotels are green building certified, up from 34 per cent in FY25. Renewable energy accounted for 39.4 per cent of energy use in FY26, compared with 17.0 per cent in FY25, against a target of 50 per cent.
